recipes.name: Irish Lamb and Potato Stew Recipe
ingredients_raw: 1 pound baking potatoes, peeled and sliced
1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley, for garnish

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
Layer lamb, onion, potatoes, carrot, and celery in an oven-proof pot or casserole dish. Season each layer with parsley, salt, and pepper as you go. Pour in beef stock and cover tightly.
Bake in the preheated oven until lamb is very tender, about 1 ½ to 2 hours. Divide into bowls and garnish with additional parsley.

raw_recipe.headline: Irish Lamb and Potato Stew Recipe
raw_recipe.description: This hearty lamb and potato stew with carrots, onion, and celery makes a comforting meal on a cold and blustery day. Tastes even better the next day!

review.reviewBody: This got 5 stars from my whole family. We loved it! I used 2 lbs. lamb, 2 lbs. red potatoes, about 7 multicolored organic carrots, 2 c. beef broth, the parsley, salt and black pepper. Eight hours on low in the slow cooker, and I served it with the Light Wheat Rolls from this website that I had frozen from last weekend. Yummy!

Sorry but this lacked flavour even with the additions I made below. I recommend only using 13 ounces of broth & even more spices then I used. I won't be making this again as I prefer my Old Fashioned Beef Stew from Better Homes & Gardens. Here's what I did: I used lamb shoulder in 2" cubes, which was very tender. I increased the carrots to 2 & 1/2 & added 1 parsnip. I used 1/2 of a large onion (6 ounced diced) in addition to the sauteed onion below. I added 1/2 teaspoon dry rosemary, 1/2 tablespoon Italian seasoning, more salt & fresh ground pepper. In dutch oven, I sauteed 1/2 of a large onion (6 ounces chopped) in 1/2 tablespoon each of butter & olive oil over med. heat, till translucent. I then added 3/4 teaspoon chopped garlic from jar & sauted it just until garlic started to smell. I added the lamb & browned it for 3 minutes. 15 minutes before serving, I removed ½ cup of broth & mixed with 2 tablespoons cornstarch, to make gravy.

There are two changes I made to this dish. First and biggest difference, I made this in my slow cooker. So I warmed up my cooker, used a liner, and layered in the lamb cubed up, salted, peppered and I added rosemary. Then the onion, potato, celery, carrot. Occasionally stopping to add salt and pepper. Last step was to add the broth, then cover and leave for about 4 hours before checking and stirring. Added a bit more broth turned up heat for two hours. In the end, it was excellent with some crusty bread. Husband loved it. My dad was happy with it too!

My family loved it! Followed the recipe - doubled the ingredients- left out the celery and added some garlic cloves. Prepared in the morning - covered and places in fridge. My 15 year old added the broth and popped it into the oven after he got home from school. We arrived an hour and half later - to a divine smelling home!!

We brown the lamb first in a little olive oil and bacon fat with garlic. We use quartered Yukon Golds instead of russets. We add a small can's worth of tomato paste as well before we put in the oven. Family favorite. Even better if you cook it, refrigerator, take off extra fat, and serve the next night.

Good basic recipe: Want to make it GREAT?? Sear the meat first, add 16oz of stout, and season with tsp of rosemary.
That'll do 'er!
I added red wine to the beef stock and used the slow cooker for 6 hours

This is a delicious stew. I bought lamb cubes at the local farm market, and removed much of the fat before preparing the stew. I sauteed the lamb cubes for a few minutes just to brown, then prepared the recipe as indicated (without the celery and parsley - didn't have either), and put all ingredients in a crock pot to cook for 8 hours on low. An hour before serving I made a slurry of flour and water, and stirred it into the juice of the stew, re-covered the pot and let it thicken slightly. YUM!

I made it with a few changes: I used leftover lamb which I added in the last ten minutes, I thickened the stew with two tablespoons of corn starch, and finally, I served it with a big tablespoon of mint chutney. I will make it again, it is absolutely delicious!

I adapted it since we do not eat wheat flour. I tried the coconut flower and almond flower, but they just don't have the right texture or reaction, so I ended up using a package of sausage gravy as the thickener, which I added at the end of the cooking cycle.
We do not eat carrots either, curving more towards the Keto lifestyle (yes, I know that the sausage gravy blew that right out of the water, but you use what you have, and we just don't buy carrots.) I subbed in Cauliflower instead, and it turned out great.

I didn't have any lamb so I substituted sweet Italian sausage which I browned in the bottom of the soup pot with the onions and some bacon fat. I drizzled in some red wine to deglaze the pot. I sliced the par-cooked sausage into coins about 1/2" thick. I cut the vegetables large and used vegetable stock seasoned with salt, pepper and Sazon' Achote Cilantro Seasoning. The broth needed some acidity so I splashed in a little red wine vinegar. I covered the pot and it all went into the 325 degree preheated oven for only about an hour because the pot was also already preheated. The meal was very easy to prepare and very flavorful. I sliced a loaf of Artisan Bread for dipping in the broth and poured a glass of Merlot. The best lamb stew I ever had.
Love this simple recipe! This was my second time making it. 1. I added 1 Parsnip. 2. I eliminated the Parsley and used Rosemary instead. Wonderful and SIMPLE!!!
We made this recipe as written with left over leg of lamb cubed as directed. It was delicious. We plan to make it again the next time we make a roast leg.
The stew was delicious. I dusted the lambing flour, salt and pepper, then browned it for a richer taste. Very good considering the ease of the slow cooker.
The flavors were delicious. I bought lamb shoulder stew meat but it had too much fat and bones. Next time I will buy will buy a boneless leg of lamb and cube it.
No changes, and we loved it!
Yes I definitely would make this dish again. I jt let the meal cook alito longer so the meat could be really tender.
I make it at least twice a month. Simply perfect, exactly as I remember eating growing up.
So easy, and family loves it.
This is pretty much how I’ve always made it, but it leaves out a main ingredient - diced tomatoes. They let you taste the lamb and still cut that gamy, greasy taste. Some garlic is nice too!
